md_name: X-ray phase-contrast microscopy of irradiated epithelial cells
md_description: This DAG describes the preparation, radiation exposure, X-ray phase-contrast microscopy acquisition, and computational image analysis of cultured human epithelial cells. It captures raw and processed image data used to quantify structural changes in organelles and cytoskeletal elements after ionizing radiation at different doses. The workflow includes sample preparation, irradiation, image correction, phase retrieval, segmentation, and cross-condition comparison using image correlation methods and analysis software.

I excluded protocol, exposure, capture, signal, and derivative fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample identifiers that could be redundant with experiment-level IDs and kept the schema limited to properties a downstream user would need to understand the starting cell material: biological source, cell type/line, species, tissue origin, and provenance of the culture. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no need to avoid overlaps with previously emitted names.

md_schema.descr: Free-text description of the biological origin of the starting material, e.g. primary culture, immortalized line, or donor-derived culture. Record at the point the cultured cells are defined in the study, before any preparation or irradiation steps.

Biological cell type represented by the starting culture, recorded before any experimental manipulation. For this study it should describe cultured human epithelial cells; use a controlled label or short text such as epithelial cell.

Name of the specific cell line if an established line was used, recorded at the root entity stage. Use a recognizable line designation format, for example HeLa, A549, or MCF-10A. Leave blank if the culture was primary and no line name applies.

Anatomical tissue or organ from which the culture was derived, if known, recorded for the starting biological material before preparation. Example: cervix, lung, breast epithelium, or skin epithelium.
Provenance category of the culture source, describing whether the cells came from a human donor, established cell line, or other source. Record at the entity level before any processing.

Passage number of the culture at the time the starting material for the study was defined. Record as an integer count of passaging events before preparation; typical values are low positive integers such as 1-30 depending on the line.

Text description of where the cultured cells were obtained, such as institutional repository, commercial vendor, or in-house culture collection. Record as provenance of the starting biological material only, not the experimental workflow.

Whether the human-derived culture came from a specified donor, anonymized donor pool, or is not applicable because the material is an established cell line. Use only for contextual provenance of the root entity.

md_schema.descr: Fixation approach used during cell preparation before irradiation and X-ray microscopy, recorded as the protocol name or short description. Example: chemical fixation or cryofixation. Record at the point the cells are prepared for imaging.

Primary fixative reagent used in the preparation protocol, recorded as the exact chemical name and, if available, supplier formulation. Example: paraformaldehyde or glutaraldehyde. Record during the preparation step only.

Concentration of the fixative reagent used during preparation, typically expressed as percent solution (w/v or v/v as reported). Record at the time fixation is performed; typical ranges for microscopy preparations are about 0.5-10 percent depending on reagent and protocol.

Duration of fixation in minutes, measured from fixative contact to fixative removal or protocol-defined end of fixation. Record during the preparation step; typical values may range from a few minutes to several hours depending on the protocol.

Medium or substrate used to mount the prepared cells for subsequent irradiation and imaging. Record the actual mounting medium or support material used at the end of sample preparation, such as glass slide, coverslip, membrane, or resin-based mount.

Orientation or configuration of the sample during mounting, if specified by the protocol. Use a controlled label to indicate how the cells were positioned for later exposure and imaging, for example flat-mounted, inverted, or membrane-mounted.

Temperature used during the preparation workflow, measured at the sample during fixation, washing, or mounting as specified by the protocol. Typical values may range from 4 to 37 Celsius depending on the preparation method.
Buffer or wash solution used during cell preparation, recorded as the buffer name or composition used before irradiation. Example: phosphate-buffered saline or HEPES buffer.
Boolean indicator of whether the prepared sample met the protocol-defined quality criteria before proceeding to irradiation, such as integrity, adherence, and mounting suitability.
Free-text notes on deviations, handling details, or special steps applied during cell preparation that are relevant for interpreting the later irradiation and imaging results.

Distance between the radiation source or beam-defining optics and the sample position during low-dose exposure, measured in millimeters at the irradiation setup. Record the configured geometric distance relevant to the exposure condition.

Quality indicator for the derived feature table, capturing issues such as missing values, failed rows, or incomplete extraction coverage in the computed result.
Free-text notes describing the content, filtering, or special handling of the derived feature table, such as inclusion/exclusion rules or aggregation choices.

cross_dose_comparison.reasoning: For the cross_dose_comparison Process node, I included only computational comparison parameters and software metadata needed to reproduce the joint analysis between low-dose, high-dose, and feature-table inputs. I excluded raw/corrected image properties because those belong to Signal nodes, and I excluded the final comparative findings because those belong to the downstream Derivative node dose_response_results. I also avoided reusing any previously generated generic processing fields by focusing on comparison-specific settings such as comparison design, statistical tests, correlation metrics, and effect-size thresholds. Since agent properties on process nodes include software name, version, and repository, I placed them here along with process-level quality indicators for the comparison workflow.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software package used to perform the cross-dose comparison and statistical analysis. Record the analysis tool running this computational process.
Version of the analysis software used for the cross-dose comparison step. Record the exact version or release identifier applied to the comparison inputs.
Repository, package source, or project location for the comparison software used in the workflow. Example: GitHub repository, internal code archive, or package registry reference.
Design used to compare structural features across dose conditions. Record whether the analysis was pairwise, multi-group, dose-response, or another comparison scheme.
Dose-condition groups included in the comparison, recorded as a concise description or controlled label set for the compared cohorts. Example: low_dose_vs_high_dose or multi-dose set.
Statistical test or model used to evaluate differences between dose conditions in the comparison step. Record the primary test applied to the feature data.

Image-correlation or association metric used in the comparison workflow, recorded as the specific metric applied to assess cross-condition similarity or divergence. Examples include Pearson, Spearman, or other correlation/scoring methods.
Threshold used to call a feature difference or correlation result meaningful in the cross-dose comparison, recorded as a numeric cutoff or decision boundary for the analysis.
Method used to correct for multiple statistical comparisons in the cross-dose analysis, recorded as the correction scheme applied to feature-level tests.
Process-level quality indicator describing whether the cross-dose comparison met expected analysis criteria, such as convergence, valid sample coverage, and interpretable statistical outputs.
Free-text notes on deviations, manual adjustments, or special handling during the cross-dose comparison that are relevant for reproducing the workflow.

dose_response_results.reasoning: For the dose_response_results Derivative node, I included only computed-result properties that describe the final comparative output itself: what it contains, its format, its size/shape, and result-level quality. I excluded upstream comparison parameters because those belong to the cross_dose_comparison Process node, and I excluded raw/corrected image and feature-table properties because those belong to earlier Signal and Derivative nodes. I also avoided adding a repeated experiment identifier or sample identifiers because those are established earlier in the DAG and should not be duplicated. The resulting schema is focused on the reusable final result artifact and the minimal descriptors needed to interpret and locate it.

md_schema.descr: Name or label of the final comparative results artefact produced by the cross-dose analysis. Example format: dose_response_summary or results_v1.
Storage format of the final comparative results artefact, recorded as the technical file or report format used to save the computed output. Example: csv, tsv, json, pdf, xlsx, or hdf5.

Number of rows in the final comparative results table, measured as the count of records present in the output if the result is tabular. Depending on the analysis, rows may correspond to features, comparisons, or summary records.
Number of columns in the final comparative results table, measured as the count of variables or summary fields present in the output if the result is tabular.
Storage path, URI, or repository location where the final comparative results artefact is kept. Record the access path for the output report or table.
Checksum or hash value used to verify integrity of the final comparative results file. Example formats include MD5, SHA-1, or SHA-256 digests.
Primary type of summary reported by the final derivative output, such as dose-response summary, structural-change summary, or radiation-damage inference report.
Boolean indicator of whether the final results artefact includes statistical summary information such as p-values, confidence intervals, or effect sizes.
Quality indicator for the final comparative output, capturing issues such as incomplete comparisons, ambiguous findings, or report generation problems in the derived result.
Free-text notes describing the content, caveats, or special handling of the final comparative results artefact, such as interpretation limits or report generation details.
